<jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Objective</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>White Catfish Ameiurus catus has been introduced to coastal watersheds across the United States. In the Penobscot River, Maine, this species has become increasingly common in upstream habitats that have been made accessible by recent dam removals. We characterized the movements of White Catfish to understand the temporal variation in their movement patterns and contextualize these findings within the recent changes in watershed connectivity.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>We captured and tagged 10 adult White Catfish (mean fork length = 271 mm) with acoustic transmitters in the lower Penobscot River in July 2022. The movements of the tagged fish were monitored through April 2023 with a large network of stationary receivers.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The tagged catfish were detected up to 6 km upstream and 31 km downstream from the release site. The total distance that was traveled by individuals ranged from 0 to 154 km during the study. Fall and spring movements were associated with changes in river flow and water temperature, but fish were relatively stationary from December through March, when at least five individuals were assumed to have overwintered in lower river tributaries.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Our results show that individual White Catfish may move considerable distances within large river systems and that these movements are potentially facilitated by changing river conditions. Collectively, this study fills a long-standing knowledge gap about the movement ecology of this species, adds context to help explain a recent increase in observations within their introduced range, and shows how changes in river conditions may be used to predict when and where these fish will move within a tidal system.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
title: Seasonal movements of nonnative White Catfish in the Penobscot River estuary
